name: Netherlands
note: Every body is examined by the treating doctor or a municipal forensic coroner; a natural death gets a verklaring van overlijden, and the cause goes to Statistics Netherlands. The death is declared to the civil registrar, usually by the undertaker under mandate and possibly electronically, before the burial permit is granted, which must be within six working days. The registrar immediately passes the death to the municipality's Basisregistratie Personen, which supplies authorised government bodies, health insurers and pension funds automatically, so the family need not tell them.

steps.title: Treating doctor or municipal coroner examines the body
steps.who: The behandelende arts, or a gemeentelijke lijkschouwer (a registered forensic physician appointed by the municipality).

deadline.text: zo spoedig mogelijk na het overlijden

steps.summary: Every body is examined (lijkschouwing). If satisfied the death was natural, the examining doctor issues a verklaring van overlijden, which the registrar needs before granting a burial or cremation permit.

steps.title: Treating doctor refers doubtful deaths to the municipal coroner
steps.who: The treating doctor who cannot issue a verklaring (also in all euthanasia/assisted-suicide cases).
steps.summary: Where the treating doctor cannot certify a natural death, he notifies the gemeentelijke lijkschouwer at once on a prescribed form.

steps.title: Municipal coroner reports a non-natural death to the public prosecutor and warns the registrar
steps.localName: verslag aan de officier van justitie
steps.who: The gemeentelijke lijkschouwer; the officier van justitie (public prosecutor) and the ambtenaar van de burgerlijke stand.
steps.trigger: Coroner cannot issue a verklaring van overlijden.
steps.summary: The prosecutor then decides whether to issue a verklaring van geen bezwaar, without which no permit is granted.

steps.title: Cause of death reported to the CBS medical officer
steps.who: The treating doctor or gemeentelijke lijkschouwer (or a doctor designated by the prosecutor in prosecutor cases).
steps.trigger: Issue of the verklaring van overlijden.

deadline.text: zo spoedig mogelijk na de afgifte van de verklaring van overlijden

steps.summary: The cause of death, with the deceased's BSN, goes on a prescribed form to the medical officer of Statistics Netherlands.

steps.title: Declare the death to the civil registrar
steps.who: Anyone with personal knowledge of the death; may mandate the person arranging the funeral (in practice the undertaker), who may declare electronically where the municipality allows it.

deadline.text: within the burial/cremation window of art. 16 Wlb (by the sixth working day)

steps.summary: The akte van overlijden is drawn up by the registrar of the municipality of death. The informant must give name, birth, place/date/time of death, civil status and last address.

steps.title: Mayor declares the death if nobody else does
steps.who: The burgemeester of the municipality where the akte must be drawn up.
steps.trigger: No authorised informant declares within the art. 16 window.

deadline.text: by the end of the burial window

steps.summary: A fallback that guarantees registration even when no relative acts.

steps.title: Registrar grants the burial or cremation permit
steps.who: The person arranging the disposal applies; the ambtenaar van de burgerlijke stand grants the verlof free of charge.
steps.trigger: Application, with the verklaring van overlijden or prosecutor's verklaring van geen bezwaar.

deadline.text: burial/cremation no earlier than 36 hours and by the sixth working day

steps.summary: No burial or cremation without the registrar's written permit, which needs the doctor's or prosecutor's statement; burial or cremation must happen between 36 hours and the sixth working day after death (the mayor can vary this).

steps.title: Extract open to anyone; full copy only with a legitimate interest
steps.who: Any person may obtain an uittreksel (extract) of the death record; an afschrift (full copy) requires a gerechtvaardigd belang.
steps.summary: Death extracts are available to everyone; full copies are restricted.

steps.title: Registrar passes the death to the municipality's BRP
steps.who: The ambtenaar van de burgerlijke stand informs the college van burgemeester en wethouders; if the deceased lived elsewhere, that municipality is told immediately.
steps.trigger: Entry of the akte van overlijden.
steps.summary: Death is a recorded item in the Basisregistratie Personen; it is taken from the akte and entered by the municipality where the person was registered.

steps.title: BRP systematically supplies authorised government bodies (afnemers)
steps.who: Government bodies authorised by a ministerial autorisatiebesluit, e.g. the Sociale Verzekeringsbank (AOW pensions), UWV and the Belastingdienst.
steps.latencyNote: geen termijn gesteld (brp-3.1; bbrp-37; Regeling BRP gelezen)
steps.summary: The register exists to supply government bodies with its data; the Minister supplies each authorised body systematically under a published autorisatiebesluit. The individual autorisatiebesluiten naming SVB, UWV and the Belastingdienst were not read.

steps.title: Tax administration receives BRP death data as an afnemer
steps.latencyNote: geen termijn gesteld (brp-3.1; bbrp-37; Regeling BRP gelezen)
steps.summary: Same mechanism as for other government afnemers; the specific autorisatiebesluit was not read.

steps.title: Health insurers receive BRP data systematically
steps.who: Zorgverzekeraars under the Zorgverzekeringswet, designated as derden for systematic supply.
steps.latencyNote: geen termijn gesteld (brp-3.3; bbrp-37; Regeling BRP gelezen)
steps.summary: Statutory health insurers are designated third parties for systematic BRP supply, so a registered death reaches them without the family.

steps.title: Pension funds and pension insurers receive BRP data systematically
steps.who: Pension funds, occupational pension funds, the Stichting Notarieel Pensioenfonds, premium pension institutions and pension insurers (Pensioenwet).
steps.latencyNote: geen termijn gesteld (brp-3.3; bbrp-37; Regeling BRP gelezen)
steps.summary: Pension providers are designated third parties for systematic BRP supply for running pension schemes.

steps.title: Banks and insurers may ask the municipality for date of death
steps.who: Banks, investment firms, insurers and investment institutions registered under the Wft, to honour claims of entitled persons.
steps.summary: Financial institutions may obtain, on request, a limited set of data including the date of death, to pay out balances and policies.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Working days, not calendar days: the aangifte must be made within the burial/cremation window of Wlb art. 16 (by the sixth working day after death), failing which the mayor declares.

informantDuty.note: Anyone with personal knowledge may declare and may mandate the person arranging the funeral (usually the undertaker); the mayor declares if no one does.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No review of every certificate; the gemeentelijke lijkschouwer (forensic physician) examines only referred, non-natural, euthanasia and child deaths.

electronicRegistration.note: A mandated informant may declare electronically where the municipality has opened that route.

governmentPropagation.note: Registrar → municipal BRP immediately; the BRP supplies authorised government bodies and designated third parties systematically.

certificateAccess.note: Extract open to anyone; full copy only with a legitimate interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: Pension funds and health insurers get systematic BRP supply; banks and insurers can request date of death.

gaps: The individual autorisatiebesluiten (Staatscourant) authorising the SVB, UWV and Belastingdienst as BRP afnemers were not read; those steps are marked unverified although the mechanism (Wet BRP arts. 3.1–3.2) is verified.
Electoral roll, passports/ID (Paspoortwet) and driving licences (RDW): no death-specific provision read; they are understood to work off the BRP but this was not sourced.
Statistics Netherlands' receipt of BRP death data (other than the cause-of-death form under Wlb art. 12a) was not sourced.
No offence for failing to declare a death was identified in BW Boek 1 art. 19h; the mayor's fallback duty substitutes for an informant offence.
No legal requirement of public notice or a notice to creditors; nothing recorded for the 'public' stage.
rijksoverheid.nl / rvig.nl guidance was not consulted; all sources are statute and AMvB on wetten.overheid.nl.
